b: If my childhood could be summed up in one dinner, this Chicken and Stuffing Casserole would be it. It was the meal my mom could make for our family of five that guaranteed instant happiness. With a box of stuffing mix and just 15 minutes of prep, you get tender, juicy chicken, a velvety homemade sauce, and a crispy, golden stuffing on top, all for just $1.28 a serving. I’ll happily make this easy, incredibly comforting casserole any time of year, so if I spot a good deal on stuffing mix around Thanksgiving, I always pick up a box to keep in the pantry for later!
A Creamy Chicken Bake With a Buttery Stuffing Top

My mom is an incredible home chef, and like any smart, busy parent, she relied on shortcuts, such as cream of chicken soup, to make dinners like this casserole easier. However, for my version, I wanted a gravy I could season myself. Making the gravy in the same skillet I use to sear the chicken breasts means the chicken broth picks up all those flavorful browned bits. The butter and flour give the gravy enough body to coat the chicken, milk makes it creamy, and a little onion and garlic powder season it without any extra chopping.

I always make stuffing from scratch for the holidays, but I like to keep a box of chicken-flavored stuffing mix in the cupboard for dinners like this. The bread is already cut and seasoned, and it soaks up the broth right in the baking dish so it stays tender underneath. I still dot the top with pats of butter so the stuffing bakes up golden and crisp (because my mom said you can’t skip this step!). Give me a corner piece with extra-crisp stuffing and plenty of gravy to scoop up with the chicken, and I’m happy. 😋 My mom actually tried my take on her chicken and stuffing casserole while visiting and told me she liked it even better than hers. That’s the highest praise to me because I’m her biggest fan!

Let the chicken sit before you flip it. I pat the 1-inch cubes dry, then give them 3 minutes undisturbed over medium-high heat. That uninterrupted contact with the hot skillet helps the underside brown and develop lots of flavor. If the pieces don’t fit in a single layer, I recommend you work in batches so trapped moisture doesn’t steam the chicken.
Drain the chicken on fresh paper towels. This helps soak up excess oil and juices that could otherwise thin the gravy in the baking dish.

Let the broth thicken before adding the milk. When you’re making the gravy, turn the heat down to medium and whisk the butter and flour for about 2 minutes so the roux can cook without scorching. Then whisk in the first cup of broth slowly to keep it smooth. I always give it about 3 minutes to thicken before adding the milk. Seeing the broth thicken at this stage is how I know the roux is doing its job.

Get the broth into the corners. Pour the remaining cup of broth evenly over the dry stuffing so you don’t end up with hard, dry patches around the edges. I also dot the top with some butter for extra flavor and browning. If you want to save a little money, you can skip those pats of butter on top if needed (it’ll still turn out delicious, just a little less browned!)

Wait before scooping. I recommend letting the casserole cool for at least 10 minutes after it comes out of the oven. If the chicken isn’t drained off well, it’ll release liquid as it cooks, which needs to be absorbed back into the dish. The sauce will also thicken during the rest, but you can still enjoy it right away if you can’t wait. Just know the sauce will be a little thinner.

Boxed stuffing already gives this casserole a head start, but if I need to get it into the oven a little sooner, I’ll check the fridge and pantry first. Leftover cooked chicken or condensed soup can save me a step and put something I already have to good use:

Use condensed soup. Replace the gravy with two small cans or one family-size can of condensed soup. My mom uses cream of chicken, and our homemade condensed soup substitutes work here too. Keep the cup of broth that goes over the stuffing.

Use rotisserie chicken. Pull the cooked meat off the bones and spread it in the baking dish in place of the seared chicken. That saves you the chopping and searing. Any shredded chicken you’ve meal prepped will work here, too.

This easy Chicken and Stuffing Casserole recipe has tender chicken, homemade gravy, and a crisp, buttery topping. Boxed stuffing keeps prep to 15 minutes!
Total Time 1 hour hour 10 minutes minutes
6 oz. box chicken flavored stuffing mix $0.97
Gather and prepare all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9×9-inch casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray; set aside.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and season evenly with ½ teaspoon of salt and ½ teaspoon of pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the cubed chicken in an even layer. Sear in batches if needed.
Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then flip, and cook for another 3 minutes. Remove the chicken from the skillet and place it on paper towels to drain. Set aside.
Turn the heat to medium and melt 4 Tbsp of butter in the skillet, then sprinkle in the flour and cook for about 2 minutes, whisking constantly.
Slowly whisk in 1 cup of chicken broth, whisk until it thickens, for about 3 minutes.
Next, whisk in the milk, remaining salt and pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder. Keep whisking until thick, for about 3 minutes. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Layer the cooked chicken on the bottom of the casserole dish in an even layer.
Spoon the sauce and spread evenly over the chicken.
Then top the casserole evenly with the stuffing mix. Pour the remaining 1 cup of chicken broth evenly over the stuffing. Dice the remaining butter into small cubes and dot on top of the stuffing.
Bake the casserole, uncovered, in the oven for about 30 minutes until golden brown. Let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.

*Feel free to try this recipe with chicken thighs! Make sure to cook chicken to an internal temperature of 165℉. If you have leftover cooked chicken, skip the searing step and add it straight to the baking dish. You can also try leftover turkey, or make our turkey and stuffing casserole if you have bone-in turkey pieces!

**I use Better Than Bouillon chicken base to make my broth because one jar makes a lot, and I can mix up just what I need. Broth and stuffing mixes vary in saltiness, so taste the gravy before spooning it over the chicken and adjust the salt as needed.

Switch up the seasonings: I use garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper to keep the flavor simple and delicious. A little paprika or a pinch of dried thyme or sage would also work if you’d like to change up the flavor. Don’t forget the stuffing topping is already seasoned!

Want to add some veggies? Chopped mushrooms, onions, carrots, or peas can help stretch the filling without much extra effort. Sauté mushrooms, onions, or carrots first and let any liquid in the skillet cook off. If you’re using frozen peas, thaw and drain them well before adding. Extra moisture can thin the gravy too much.

Make it ahead: You can make this easy chicken stuffing casserole ahead of time! Assemble the entire casserole (up to the baking step), cover it tightly, and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Let it sit on the counter while the oven preheats, and add a few extra minutes to the baking time to warm through.

Gather all your ingredients: Preheat the oven to 350°F and coat a 9×9-inch casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray. I also like to measure the chicken broth into two 1-cup portions now, so I have one ready for the gravy and one for the stuffing.

Season the chicken: Cut 2 lbs. chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes and pat them dry with paper towels. Sprinkle evenly with ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper. Drying the surface helps the chicken brown better when it hits the hot skillet.

Sear the chicken: Heat 1 Tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When the oil shimmers, add the chicken in a single layer. You should hear it sizzle as it goes in. Work in batches if needed. Leave the chicken undisturbed for 3 minutes to brown on the underside. Flip the pieces and cook for another 3 minutes, then transfer them to a plate lined with fresh paper towels to catch any excess oil and juices.

Make the roux: Reduce the heat to medium and melt 4 Tbsp butter in the same skillet. Sprinkle in ½ cup flour and whisk constantly for about 2 minutes. The flour and butter should come together into a smooth paste.

Add the broth: Now slowly pour in 1 cup chicken broth, whisking as you go to keep the mixture smooth and loosen the browned bits from the skillet. Keep whisking for about 3 minutes, until the broth has visibly thickened.
Finish the gravy: Whisk in 1 cup milk, the remaining ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp onion powder, and ½ tsp garlic powder.
Keep whisking for about 3 minutes, until the gravy is smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Turn off the heat.
Layer the chicken in the dish: Spread the seared chicken in an even layer across the bottom of the prepared casserole dish so each scoop gets some chicken.
Cover the chicken with gravy: Spoon the gravy over the chicken and use the back of the spoon to spread it all the way to the edges.
Add the stuffing topping: Scatter one 6 oz. box of dry chicken-flavored stuffing mix evenly over the gravy.
Pour over the broth: Slowly pour the remaining 1 cup chicken broth over the entire surface, including the corners, so there are no dry patches.
Add the butter: Cut the remaining 2 Tbsp butter into small cubes and dot them across the top for a buttery finish.

Bake and let it rest: Bake uncovered for about 30 minutes, until the stuffing is golden brown and the center of the casserole and the larger pieces of chicken near the center reach 165°F. Let it rest for 10 minutes before scooping so the gravy has a chance to settle. Serve and enjoy!
What to Serve with Chicken and Stuffing Casserole

I like a little crunch on the side when dinner comes with this much gravy. Our sautéed green beans are crisp and garlicky, and you can make them on the stovetop while the casserole bakes. If you’ve already got a bag of broccoli in the freezer, oven-roasted frozen broccoli is an inexpensive side with no chopping, and a simple side salad with a tangy vinaigrette helps balance the rich gravy. Or if I’m feeding a few extra people, I’ll sometimes add a batch of homemade biscuits to help stretch the meal further. Split one open and use it to mop up the gravy left on your plate!
How to Make a Simple Side Salad
Divide leftovers into shallow, airtight containers and refrigerate within 2 hours. They’ll keep in the fridge for 3-4 days. Keep in mind the topping can soften, and the sauce will thicken in storage.

Warm refrigerated portions in an oven-safe dish at 350°F until the center reaches 165°F. Cover loosely with foil to keep the chicken and gravy from drying out, then uncover for the last few minutes to help crisp up the stuffing. You can also microwave a single portion in short bursts, though the topping will be softer.

I prefer to freeze individual portions in airtight, freezer-safe containers (for up to 3 months). Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat at 350°F as directed above. The stuffing will soften a little after freezing, so reheating it in the oven is worth the extra time if you like a crisp top.
